info.title: AstroMansion API
info.description: Astrology calculation API: natal charts, transits, returns, synastry, traditional and predictive techniques, powered by our own in-house astronomical core with arcsecond precision.

get.description: Return candidate places for the birth-location selector.

post.description:
Calculate the free natal chart response.

The response includes the big three, planets, aspects, and optionally the
chart wheel. The SVG wheel is returned only when ``wheel=true``. Otherwise
the response is data-only and omits the ``wheel`` field. ``include`` and
``exclude`` can narrow the planet set within the free subset. ``title``
heads the wheel. ``author`` signs it, and when it is left empty a
signed-in app session signs with its account's chosen name, or leaves the
wheel unsigned when the account has none.
Calculate exact Saturn return dates from birth data.

get.description: Return every lunar phase in a calendar year.

post.summary: Lunar phase query filtered by month and phase
post.description:
Return detailed machine output with optional month and phase filters.

This developer endpoint does not use birth data. ``GET /moon-phases``
returns a concise localized annual calendar, while this POST endpoint also
exposes ``jd`` and ``lon`` fields and supports month and phase filters.

post.summary: MansionSQL query over a calculated chart
post.description:
Run MansionSQL against a calculated chart.

Without ``format``, the endpoint returns the standard JSON envelope. With
a format, it returns plain text designed for terminal use through ``curl``.
Embedding a rendered table in JSON would make escape sequences unreadable.

post.summary: Chart wheel SVG with optional interactive HTML
post.description: Render a chart wheel as SVG or interactive HTML.
Render a chart wheel as PNG.
Render a story card for one chart or for two.
Render an astrocartography map as one self-contained SVG.
Render a bi-wheel SVG with natal and outer charts.
Export a chart as a PDF report.
Export the chart body table as CSV.

Build an editable, brandable, multi-page natal PDF report.

Plans with ``Scope.EXPORT`` receive PDF export. A signed-in app session
without it may spend a report credit instead, the same credits the
website's report studio spends: one credit buys the report for one chart,
is charged only once the document exists, and a chart already paid for is
drawn again for free. Developer keys never spend credits.

Hiding the AstroMansion brand or embedding a custom logo additionally
requires ``Scope.WHITE_LABEL``. The plan that grants it is read from
``TierConstants``, so the error, the schema, and the pricing page name the same
plan. A request without that scope is rejected with 403 rather than
silently ignored: a machine caller cannot see a dropped field, and would
ship a branded document it never got. The engine output is already
unbranded. White-label access means applying the caller's brand.

post.description:
Run multiple techniques sequentially in one request.

Every item receives an independent scope check. Invalid or unauthorized
items do not stop the remaining work and appear as errors in the results.

post.summary: Save and calculate a named custom Keplerian body
post.description:
Calculate a custom body and optionally save it under its owner's identity.

Saved bodies can be calculated later through
``POST /v1/custom-body/{name}`` without resubmitting orbital elements. The
API-key identity digest owns the stored record.

get.description: Return every custom body saved by the current identity.

post.summary: Calculate a saved custom body by name
post.description:
Calculate an owned custom body by name for the supplied birth data.

Orbital elements do not need to be resubmitted after the body has been
saved.

delete.description: Delete an owned custom body by name.

get.description: Return lightweight job summaries for the current identity.

post.summary: Create an async job for any technique
post.description:
Queue one technique for background execution.

The scope, request body, and optional callback URL are validated before the
job is stored. The endpoint returns HTTP 202 when the pending-job limit has
not been reached. Poll the result through ``GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}``.

post.summary: Create an async job batch of up to 20 items
post.description:
Queue multiple jobs in one request.

Each item receives independent scope and body validation. An invalid item
does not stop the others and appears as an error in the result list. Every
successful job consumes quota independently.

get.description:
Return a job's status and its result after completion.

The identity embedded in the key enforces ownership. Jobs owned by another
identity are not visible and therefore return 404 without disclosing their
existence.

Confirm that the API can serve, without invoking domain services.

Every call checks its key and counts against its limits in the cache,
so the API is unavailable while the cache does not answer.

NatalApiOptions.title: NatalApiOptions
NatalApiOptions.description:
How the public natal answer is drawn, and which planets it keeps.

``title`` heads the wheel in place of the natal chart heading, as a chart
cast for a return is not a birth chart. ``author`` signs the wheel. Left
empty, a signed-in app session signs with the name its account chose and
any other caller signs anonymously.

NatalApiRequest.title: NatalApiRequest
NatalApiRequest.description:
The public natal request: a birth and the options that shape the answer.

The deprecated flat body, ``NatalRequest``'s fields at the top level, is
still read, by ``NatalRequest``'s rules, and ``flat_shape`` tells the
route to mark the answer with a ``Deprecation`` header::

    body holds "birth"   ──► read as it stands
    body without it      ──► read as NatalRequest, moved under "birth"
                             and "options", flat_shape set

ShareCardRequest.title: ShareCardRequest
ShareCardRequest.description:
A story card for one chart or for two.

One card, two subjects. ``type`` picks which: the synastry card reads
both charts and leads on their compatibility score, the natal card reads
``birth`` alone and leads on its Sun, Moon, and Ascendant. Splitting them
across two paths would have published one product as two.
